newsitem.title: USA: Militia leader convicted in West Virginia trial.
newsitem.headline: Militia leader convicted in West Virginia trial.

text.p: The self-described leader of a West Virginia militia was convicted Friday of conspiracy to engage in manufacturing and dealing in explosives without a license, U.S. attorney William Wilmoth said.

Floyd Raymond Looker, self-described general of the Mountaineer Militia, was convicted after a four-day trial in U.S. District Court in Wheeling, W.V., on the first of four indictments in a case that involved an alleged plot to blow up the FBI's national fingerprint centre.
The charge carries a maximum sentence of five years in jail and a $250,000 fine. Two of Looker's co-defendants, Jack Phillips and Edward Moore, entered guilty pleas.
Looker and six others were arrested last October after an FBI undercover investigation. They were indicted on charges of plotting to plant bombs at the fingerprint facility in Clarksburg, W.V.
